specPoints.text: understand how to interpret family pedigrees

primer.text: A pedigree is inheritance written as a family portrait. This note teaches the symbol code — squares, circles, shading, marriage lines — and shows how counsellors read the chart to trace a characteristic through the generations and estimate who is likely to carry it next.

lessons.title: Reading the Family Chart
lessons.opening: A family pedigree maps a trait, usually a disorder, across the generations of one family, and reading the symbols lets you judge who carries the characteristic and estimate the probability that a particular relative has inherited it.
keyPoints: Squares mark males and circles mark females.
Red shading marks affected individuals; blue marks the unaffected.
A horizontal line between a couple records children they produced.
Pedigrees trace inheritance patterns through many generations at once.

low.restatement: The chart shows who has the trait, who might pass it on, and how it travelled down the family.
low.analogy: A family tree where the fruit you are studying is coloured in.
low.examPointer: Memorise the symbol code; questions usually start with a straight symbol read.

medium.restatement: Shading plus lines reveal which branch carries the disorder and let you infer hidden genotypes.
medium.analogy: Reading a metro map: the stations are people, the lines are descent, the highlighted stations show the trait.
medium.examPointer: Support any probability answer by citing the genotypes the chart implies.

check.stem: Which shape denotes a male in a pedigree chart?

options.explanation: Right — the other options each misplace a concept.
Circles mark females.
Triangles are not used in the taught code.
No diamond appears in the taught convention.

check.stem: What does a horizontal line joining two individuals mean?

options.explanation: Right — the other options each misplace a concept.
Siblings hang from the same vertical drop, not a joining line.
Shading, not lines, marks the affected.
The line records offspring, not outside marriage.

check.stem: Affected individuals appear in which colour in the taught convention?

options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.
Blue marks the unaffected.
The taught chart uses red and blue.
Green plays no part in the convention.

check.stem: Why are pedigrees drawn across several generations?

options.text: To reveal the pattern of inheritance of the characteristic
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.

options.text: To count chromosomes in each person
options.explanation: Pedigrees record traits, not chromosome counts.
Height is not what the chart tracks.
Cell division timing never appears on a pedigree.

check.stem: A pedigree shows two unaffected parents with an affected child. What does that suggest about the trait?

options.text: It can hide in carriers, hinting at a recessive pattern
options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.
Hidden passage through carriers is a genetic pattern.
A dominant trait usually shows in a parent.
No one invents an inherited genotype.

check.stem: State what a family pedigree is used for.
check.modelAnswer: It traces the pattern of inheritance of a characteristic, usually a disorder, through the generations of a family.

check.stem: List the symbol conventions of a pedigree chart.
check.modelAnswer: Squares for males, circles for females, red for affected and blue for unaffected individuals.

check.stem: Explain how a pedigree can support a probability estimate for a relative.
check.modelAnswer: The chart shows which relatives express the trait, letting you infer genotypes and calculate the chance that a given family member inherited the disorder.

check.stem: In the taught chart, one family group shows no affected parents and no affected children, while other groups show affected parents and affected children. Describe what this contrast tells a genetic counsellor.
check.modelAnswer: The unaffected group suggests the trait is absent or hidden in that branch, while the affected groups show it passing from parent to child, so the counsellor can target advice at the branches carrying it.

glossary.definition: A diagram tracing one characteristic through the generations of a family.
An individual showing the characteristic being traced, drawn shaded red here.
An individual who holds an allele without showing its characteristic.
